mainTopic: Which Temple fund pays for the כלי שרת, and whether הקדש money may be used to make a profit
overview: רב הונא asks רב whether the Temple's כלי שרת may be paid for with בדק הבית money, or only from תרומת הלשכה. רב rules: only from תרומת הלשכה. A פסוק in דברי הימים seems to show repair money used for vessels, but רב answers with a פסוק in מלכים that says the repair money went to the workers. The גמרא settles the clash between the two פסוקים: only money left over after the repairs went to vessels, because בית דין silently made that condition from the start. A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל supports רב, reading 'הכסף' as the first money, the main תרומת הלשכה. Another ברייתא says כלי שרת come from מותר נסכים. The גמרא answers that this is a dispute between תנאים, and quotes a משנה with the views of רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא. It then explains רבי ישמעאל's 'leftover produce' as profit from trading with leftover money. רבי עקיבא rejects this, because he forbids making profits with הקדש money or with charity money. Finally the גמרא returns to our משנה about a husband who went overseas, and begins רב's opinion, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can upkeep money pay for Temple service vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The question is asked whether כלי שרת may be made from בדק הבית funds. The two sides are spelled out: are the vessels a need of the מזבח, or a need of the קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about service vessels: may they be made from money set aside for Temple upkeep? Do they count as a need of the altar, so they come from upkeep money? Or do they count as a need of the offerings, so they were made from the treasury-chamber fund?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks רב a question about which Temple fund pays for the service vessels. He lays out the two possible ways of looking at them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate funds. בדק הבית money pays for the building and the מזבח. תרומת הלשכה (the half-shekel collection) pays for the communal קרבנות. The question is which group the vessels belong to: are they part of the Temple's 'structure', or are they tools of the offerings?

keyTerms.meaning: Service vessels used in the Temple's עבודה
Money given for the upkeep and repair of the Temple building
A need of the altar (part of the Temple structure)
A need of the offerings themselves
The communal fund from the half-shekel, kept in the Temple chamber

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole סוגיא depends on this either/or. Vessels that 'belong to' the קרבנות must be paid for from the communal offering fund.

phrases.english: Service vessels, what is the law
about making them from money consecrated for Temple upkeep?
Are they a need of the altar,
and so they come from Temple-upkeep money?
Or are they a need of the offerings,
and so they would make them from the chamber collection?
phrases.notes: This is the half-shekel money that everyone gave, which paid for the communal קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מַהוּ שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ מִקׇּדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כלי שרת are classified as צורך מזבח (funded by בדק הבית) or צורך קרבן (funded by תרומת הלשכה).

steps.title: רב rules: only from the treasury chamber
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that כלי שרת are made only from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They are made only from the chamber collection.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a clear answer to the question. The vessels are paid for only by the communal offering fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב takes the second side of the question. The vessels count as a need of the קרבנות. So בדק הבית money may not be used for them.

keyTerms.meaning: They are made only from

phrases.english: He said to him: They are not made
except from the chamber collection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין נַעֲשִׂין אֶלָּא מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלי שרת are צורך קרבן and are made only from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Challenge from the פסוק in דברי הימים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a פסוק showing that leftover upkeep money was used to make כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'And when they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and יהוידע, and he made it into vessels for the house of ה׳, service vessels...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא attacks רב's ruling with a פסוק. In that פסוק, money collected for repairing the Temple was used to make service vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the time of יהוידע, the money was collected to fix the Temple, so it was בדק הבית money. Yet the פסוק says that the rest of it was made into כלי שרת. That seems to prove that upkeep money can pay for vessels, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder of the money
The כהן גדול who led the Temple repairs in the days of King יואש

phrases.english: He objected: "And when they had finished, they brought before the king
and Jehoiada the rest of the money,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The פסוק itself doesn't say it.

phrases.english: and he made it into vessels for the house of ה׳,
service vessels, etc."!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that כלי שרת come only from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows money from the Temple-repair collection (בדק הבית) being used to make כלי שרת.

steps.title: רב answers from the פסוק in מלכים
steps.stepSummary: רב answers sharply that רב הונא forgot the parallel פסוק in נביאים. That פסוק says the repair money was not made into vessels but was given to the workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whoever taught you the Writings did not teach you the Prophets: 'But there were not made for the house of ה׳ cups... for they gave it to those who did the work.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his ruling with a different פסוק. That פסוק says the repair money was NOT used for vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same story appears in ספר מלכים. There it says plainly that no vessels were made from the money; it all went to the workers. So רב has a פסוק that fits his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught you to read
The Writings (כתובים), which include דברי הימים
The Prophets (נביאים), which include מלכים
The workers doing the repairs

phrases.english: He said to him: Whoever taught you the Writings
did not teach you the Prophets:

phrases.aramaic: ״אַךְ לֹא יֵעָשֶׂה בֵּית ה׳ סִפּוֹת וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: "But there were not made for the house of ה׳ cups, etc.
for they gave it to those who did the work."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאַקְרְיָיךְ כְּתוּבֵי לָא אַקְרְיָיךְ נְבִיאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 with a contrary פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-source: a parallel פסוק that supports the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in דברי הימים proves that upkeep money pays for vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק in מלכים says the upkeep money was not used for vessels, which supports רב.

steps.title: The two verses seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that, according to this, the פסוק in דברי הימים and the פסוק in מלכים contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verses contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem that comes out of רב's answer. One פסוק says vessels were made from the money, and the other says they were not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's answer defends his ruling, but it leaves the two פסוקים clashing about the same event. The גמרא needs a way to make both true.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The verses contradict one another

phrases.english: If so, the verses contradict each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the clash between the פסוקים of steps 3 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in דברי הימים against the פסוק in מלכים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says the money was made into vessels; the other says it was not.

steps.title: Leftover money versus no leftover
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים are describing different situations. When the collection had money left over, the extra went to vessels. When nothing was left over, it all went to the workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, they collected and had money left over. There, they collected and had nothing left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying each פסוק describes a different stage. The difference is whether there was leftover money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלכים describes the time when the money was still needed for repairs, so none went to vessels. The פסוק in דברי הימים says 'the rest of the money', which means only the leftover after the work was done. Only leftover upkeep money may go to vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
That they collected
They had money left over

steps.whatToRemember: רב: כלי שרת are paid for from תרומת הלשכה. The פסוק in דברי הימים talks only about leftover repair money, while the פסוק in מלכים talks about money still needed for the repairs.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that בדק הבית money normally pays for vessels. It only explains the leftover case described in the פסוק.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where they collected and had some left over,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the פסוק in דברי הימים, which speaks of 'the rest of the money'.

phrases.english: there, where they collected and had nothing left over.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן שֶׁגָּבוּ וְהוֹתִירוּ, כָּאן שֶׁגָּבוּ וְלֹא הוֹתִירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים describe the same use of the money and so contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leftover collected money could go to vessels; when nothing was left over, all of it went to the workers.

steps.title: How can leftover repair money be used for vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if money was left over from the repair collection, it was given for repairs. So how could it be used for כלי שרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they collected and had some left over, so what? (That money was still given for repairs!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 6. Money given for one purpose should not be switched to a different purpose just because some is left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said that when the repair collection had extra money, the extra went to vessels. The problem is that the people gave that money specifically for בדק הבית (repairing the building). Having extra does not obviously allow it to be moved to a different holy use.

keyTerms.meaning: They collected (the money)
They had some left over
So what? What difference does that make?
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And if they collected and had some left over,
what of it?
phrases.notes: He means: that money was still given for repairs, so being 'extra' shouldn't let you spend it on vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6 (leftover repair money went to vessels).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that leftover repair-collection money was used for כלי שרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money given for repairs is set aside for repairs. Having extra does not by itself allow it to be moved to a different purpose.

steps.title: בית דין makes a silent condition on the money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that בית דין has a built-in condition on the repair money from the start. If it is needed for repairs, it is used for repairs; if not, it goes to כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: בית דין has it in mind as a condition on the money. If it is needed, it is needed; and if not, it will be for the service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers step 7's question. The leftover could go to vessels because that was the plan from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money was never set aside only for repairs. בית דין, which is in charge of the public funds, silently attached a condition when the money came in. So using the extra for vessels is not a switch; it follows the original terms.

keyTerms.meaning: בית דין makes a condition in its mind (an unspoken condition)
They were needed
The service vessels of the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'לב בית דין מתנה' (an unspoken condition by בית דין on public holy funds) explains how leftover communal money can be redirected without breaking the original purpose.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The heart of the court stipulates about them:
phrases.notes: Literally 'the heart' of בית דין. He means a condition they hold in mind without saying it out loud.

phrases.english: If they are needed [for repairs], they are needed;
and if not, they will be for the service vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a legal mechanism: an unspoken condition made by בית דין from the start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repair money is locked to repairs and cannot be moved to vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: From the start the money came with a condition: repairs if needed, otherwise vessels.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב from 'the rest of the money'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that כלי שרת come from תרומת הלשכה. They learn it from the פסוק 'the rest of the money', since that is the fund that has a remainder.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: service vessels come from תרומת הלשכה, as it says 'the rest of the money'. Which money has a remainder? You must say it is תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב's original ruling from step 2. It reads the same פסוק in דברי הימים (about leftover money) as pointing to תרומת הלשכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the rest of the money' assume a fund that is used up partly and has something left over. תרומת הלשכה fits this: part of it is used for the offerings, and the rest is left. So the vessels mentioned in that פסוק were paid for by תרומת הלשכה, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)
The funds taken out of the Temple chamber (from the half-shekel collection)
Leftovers, a remainder
You must say (only one answer fits)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Service vessels come from the collection of the chamber,
as it is stated: “The rest of the money.”
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 24:14, the same פסוק רב הונא used back in step 3.

phrases.english: Which money has a remainder?
You must say: this is the collection of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת בָּאִין מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the repair-money discussion and brings tannaitic support for רב's main ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that כלי שרת are paid for from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל, reading the פסוק 'את שאר הכסף' (דברי הימים ב 24:14).

steps.title: Maybe the vessels come from the leftover itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not say the vessels were paid for by the leftover money itself, and not by the main תרומת הלשכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the leftovers themselves (paid for the vessels)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the ברייתא's reading. The פסוק says 'the rest', so maybe it means the remainder itself was used for vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used 'the rest of the money' only to identify which fund is meant. But the plain words could mean that the vessels came from the leftover portion (שירי הלשכה), not from the main fund. If so, the proof for רב no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (offering a different reading)
Themselves

phrases.english: But say the remainder itself?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the vessels were bought with the leftover money, not with the main chamber fund.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 9 reads the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'שאר הכסף' points to the main תרומת הלשכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'The rest' could simply mean the leftover portion itself, so the vessels might come from the remainder rather than the main fund.

steps.title: 'The money' means the first money, like רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבא's rule. Just as 'העולה' (with 'the') means the first עולה, 'הכסף' means the first money, which is the main תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'the burnt-offering' means the first burnt-offering. So too 'the money' means the first money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא's reading. The little word 'the' (ה׳) points to the first, main money, not the leftover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא taught elsewhere that the extra 'ה' in 'העולה' points to the first עולה of the day. The same reading applies here: 'הכסף' points to the first money taken out, which is תרומת הלשכה itself. So the vessels come from the main fund, as רב said; the word 'rest' only shows which fund has a remainder.

keyTerms.meaning: As רבא said (bringing an earlier teaching)
The first burnt-offering
So too, the same here

steps.whatToRemember: The 'ה' in 'הכסף' points to the first money, the main תרומת הלשכה. So the ברייתא stands as support for רב: כלי שרת come from תרומת הלשכה.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
“The burnt-offering” means the first burnt-offering;
so too, “the money” means the first money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a word, using a parallel rule from רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The rest of the money' means the vessels were paid for by the leftover itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכסף' with 'the' means the first money, so the vessels came from the main תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says vessels come from leftover libation money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא. It says the קטורת and public offerings come from תרומת הלשכה, but the golden מזבח, לבונה and כלי שרת come from מותר נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The incense and all public offerings come from תרומת הלשכה. The golden altar, frankincense and service vessels come from the leftover money of the libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רב and to the school of רבי ישמעאל from a ברייתא. Step 14 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא sorts the expenses. Offerings and קטורת are paid for by תרומת הלשכה, while כלי שרת are listed with the items paid for by מותר נסכים (leftover libation money). That directly contradicts רב's ruling that כלי שרת come from תרומת הלשכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense offered in the בית המקדש
Offerings brought for the whole community
The golden altar inside the היכל
Leftover money from the funds for wine libations

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lists. The קטורת itself comes from תרומת הלשכה, but the golden altar it is burned on comes from מותר נסכים.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The incense and all communal offerings
come from the collection of the chamber;
the golden altar, the frankincense, and the service vessels
come from the leftover of the libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא's support is secured in step 11, a different ברייתא is brought against רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling (step 2) and the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל (step 9) that כלי שרת come from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists כלי שרת among the items paid for by מותר נסכים, not by תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes its list: altar, courtyards, and the city's needs
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the ברייתא from the challenge. The outer altar, the chambers and the courtyards are paid for from בדק הבית money. Things outside the courtyard wall, like Jerusalem's wall and towers, come from the leftovers of the לשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The altar of burnt-offerings, the chambers and the courtyards are paid for with money given for Temple repairs. Things outside the courtyard wall are paid for with the leftovers of the chambers. This is what we learned: the city wall, its towers and all the city's needs are paid for with the leftovers of the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא it used to challenge רב in the last step. It finishes the list of which fund pays for what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part does not add a new attack. It completes the ברייתא's chart of funds: building parts go to בדק הבית, and city needs go to the leftover לשכה money. The real force of the challenge is still the earlier line, which says כלי שרת come from מותר נסכים and not from תרומת הלשכה, as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar, where most offerings were burned
Money given for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
The leftover money in the Temple treasury chamber
The wall of Jerusalem

phrases.english: The altar of burnt-offerings, the chambers, and the courtyards —
come from money consecrated for Temple repairs.
Things outside the wall of the courtyard —
come from the leftovers of the chambers.
phrases.notes: He means the money left over in the Temple treasury chamber after the public offerings were paid for.

phrases.english: This is what we learned:
The city wall and its towers
and all the needs of the city
come from the leftovers of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the ברייתא quoted in step 12 as a challenge to רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that כלי שרת are bought from תרומת הלשכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The full ברייתא lists every fund and assigns כלי שרת to מותר נסכים, not to תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים: the משנה about the leftover collection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this question is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a משנה: the first opinion says the leftover collection money was used for gold plating in the קודש הקדשים. רבי ישמעאל says the leftover produce went to קיץ המזבח, and the leftover collection went to כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as we learned in a משנה: what would they do with the leftover of the collection? They made hammered gold plates to coat the קודש הקדשים. רבי ישמעאל says: the leftover produce went to extra offerings for the altar, and the leftover collection went to כלי שרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing that other תנאים agree with him. It begins quoting a משנה from שקלים that records different views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is only one opinion, so it cannot disprove רב. רבי ישמעאל clearly says the leftover תרומה, meaning the שקלים collection, pays for כלי שרת, which is exactly what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is a dispute between תנאים': each side has a תנא behind it
The leftover of the שקלים collection
Thin hammered plates of gold
Extra עולות offered when the altar would otherwise be idle
'Leftover produce': profit from trading in produce (explained in step 17)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תרומה' does not mean the כהן's portion of produce. It means the collection of שקלים in the לשכה.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between תנאים,
as we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה, מָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ?
phrases.english: The leftover of the collection: what would they do with it?
Hammered gold plates
as a coating for the Holy of Holies.
רבי ישמעאל says:
The leftover produce goes to the 'קיץ' of the altar.
phrases.notes: These are extra עולות brought so the altar is never left empty.

phrases.english: The leftover collection goes to service vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 12-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: רב follows a different תנא than the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to disprove רב completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב agrees with רבי ישמעאל, who says the leftover collection pays for כלי שרת. The ברייתא follows a different view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a very common way the גמרא defends an אמורא: it shows his view is backed by a תנא, so a ברייתא with the other view does not refute him.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא give their views
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the leftover collection goes to קיץ המזבח and the leftover נסכים go to כלי שרת. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says the opposite. Neither of them accepts רבי ישמעאל's idea of 'leftover produce'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the leftover collection goes to the extra altar offerings, and the leftover libations go to כלי שרת. רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול, says: the leftover libations go to the extra altar offerings, and the leftover collection goes to כלי שרת. Neither of them agreed about the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the same משנה, now giving the rest of the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says כלי שרת come from מותר נסכים, which matches the ברייתא used against רב. רבי חנינא says they come from the leftover collection, which supports רב just as רבי ישמעאל does. So both sides of the dispute have תנאים behind them.

keyTerms.meaning: Money left over from the fund for wine libations
The deputy כהן גדול
They did not agree

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says:
The leftover collection goes to the 'קיץ' of the altar,
the leftover libations go to service vessels.
רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול, says:
The leftover libations go to the 'קיץ' of the altar,
the leftover collection goes to service vessels.

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה וָזֶה, לֹא הָיוּ מוֹדִים בְּפֵירוֹת.
phrases.english: And this one and that one did not agree about the produce.
phrases.notes: Both רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא reject רבי ישמעאל's category of 'leftover produce'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה לְקֵיץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 14 and lays out both sides of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: כלי שרת come from מותר נסכים (like the ברייתא). רבי חנינא: כלי שרת come from מותר תרומה (like רב).

steps.title: What is the 'produce' רבי ישמעאל mentioned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל meant by 'leftover produce'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'produce'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what a strange term in the משנה means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never said that the Temple had produce. So the גמרא asks where this 'leftover produce' came from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?

phrases.english: 'Produce': what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי ישמעאל's term from step 14.

steps.title: The produce is trade profit from the leftover collection
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that they used the leftover collection money to buy produce cheaply and sell it at a higher price. The profit paid for קיץ המזבח, and that profit is the 'leftover produce' in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: what would they do with the leftover collection? They bought produce cheaply and sold it at a higher price, and they used the profit for the extra altar offerings. This is what we learned: the leftover produce goes to the extra altar offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that explains 'produce' as a trading business run with the leftover money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Leftover produce' is not a separate gift of fruit. It is the profit made by trading with the leftover collection money. According to רבי ישמעאל, that profit paid for the extra altar offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Cheaply
At a high price
The profit
They provide the 'קיץ', the extra offerings, for the altar

steps.whatToRemember: Whether כלי שרת come from the leftover collection is a dispute between תנאים. רב follows רבי ישמעאל and רבי חנינא, and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא. רבי ישמעאל's 'leftover produce' means profit from trading with the leftover money.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה מָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ?
phrases.english: The leftover of the collection: what would they do with it?
They buy produce cheaply
and sell it at a high price,
and with the profit they provide the 'קיץ' for the altar.
And this is what we learned:
The leftover produce goes to the 'קיץ' of the altar.
phrases.notes: This is רבי ישמעאל's line from the משנה in step 14, now explained.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה מָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Produce' means the profit from buying produce cheaply with the leftover collection money and selling it at a higher price. That profit paid for קיץ המזבח.

steps.title: Why did the other two reject the 'leftover produce'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים did not agree with רבי ישמעאל about the 'leftover produce.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'this one and that one did not agree about the produce'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. Now that we know what 'leftover produce' means, why did רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא not accept it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 explained that 'leftover produce' is the profit from buying and selling with the leftover collection money. So the question now is why the other two תנאים rejected this kind of profit. The גמרא is setting up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one. Here it means רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
Agreed (with someone's opinion)
Produce. Here it means the profit made from trading with the leftover money.

phrases.english: What is [the reason that] "this one and that one
phrases.notes: This is quoting the line from step 15 about רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: did not agree regarding the produce"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״זֶה וָזֶה לֹא הָיוּ מוֹדִין בְּפֵירוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 defined 'leftover produce,' this step asks why the other תנאים rejected it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים did not accept profit made from the leftover collection money.

steps.title: A משנה shows רבי עקיבא forbids profit from הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: רבי ישמעאל says they bought wine, oil and flour with the leftover money and the profit went to הקדש. רבי עקיבא says you may not make a profit with הקדש money or with money for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: What would they do with the leftover money of the chamber? They would buy wine, oil and fine flour with it, and the profit went to הקדש. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: You may not make a profit with הקדש money, and not with money of the poor either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a משנה. It shows that רבי עקיבא holds a basic rule: you may not use הקדש money to make a profit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל allows trading with the leftover לשכה money, which is exactly where his 'leftover produce' came from. רבי עקיבא forbids this kind of trading, so for him there can be no 'leftover produce' at all. That is why he did not accept רבי ישמעאל's idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Wines, oils and fine flours, the things people needed for their קרבנות
Profit
Make a profit, earn money by trading

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שכר' means profit from trading, not 'wages' or 'reward.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבי עקיבא's rule that you do not make business profits with הקדש money or with charity money. רבי ישמעאל disagrees and allows trading with the leftover לשכה money.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
The leftover remainder of the chamber,
what would they do with it?
They would buy wines, oils and fine flours with it,
phrases.notes: They then sold these to people who needed them for their own קרבנות.

phrases.english: and the profit went to the Temple treasury,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
One may not make a profit with Temple property,
and not with money of the poor either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by quoting a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא holds that you may not make a profit with הקדש money, so profit from the leftover collection, the 'leftover produce,' cannot exist for him.

steps.title: The reasons behind רבי עקיבא's two rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: no profit with הקדש because the Temple should not act like a poor person; no profit with charity money because a poor person may come when all the money is tied up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not with הקדש? Because there is no poverty in a place of wealth. Why not with money of the poor? Because perhaps a poor person will come along and there will be nothing to give him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers its own question, explaining the reason for each half of רבי עקיבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הקדש, chasing small profits looks like poverty, and that does not fit the honor of the בית המקדש. For charity, the money must always be ready for the poor. If it is tied up in business, a poor person could come and go away with nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
There is no poverty in a place of wealth. The בית המקדש should not act in a cheap or needy way.
Perhaps
Happens to come along

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא forbids trading for profit with הקדש money because of the honor of the בית המקדש. He forbids it with charity money because the poor must always be able to get help right away. This is why he rejects רבי ישמעאל's 'leftover produce.'

phrases.english: With Temple property, what is the reason one may not?
There is no poverty in a place of wealth.
phrases.notes: Making small profits is how poor people act, and that does not fit the rich and honored בית המקדש.

phrases.english: With money of the poor, what is the reason one may not?
Perhaps a poor person will come along to them
and there will be nothing to give him.
phrases.notes: That is, the money is tied up in the business deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind רבי עקיבא's ruling quoted in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No profit with הקדש because 'there is no poverty in a place of wealth.' No profit with charity money because a poor person may come and there would be nothing to give him.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a man who went overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה about a man who went overseas, and begins quoting a dispute that starts with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who went overseas.' It was stated: רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of Temple money and goes back to our משנה about a husband who went overseas. It is setting up a dispute, and רב's words continue in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a brand-new section. The words 'מי שהלך למדינת הים' quote our משנה, where the wife asks for support while her husband is away. 'איתמר' tells us אמוראים argued about this case. רב's opinion comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas, a far-away land

phrases.english: One who went overseas.
phrases.notes: These words quote our משנה, about a husband far away whose wife asks for food and support.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם. אִיתְּמַר, רַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of Temple money and returns to the main משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a dispute between אמוראים, starting with רב, about the משנה's case of a husband who went overseas. רב's ruling is in the next part.
